verified.exploit_entry_point: The project's own pytest harness (notebook.tests.launchnotebook.NotebookTestBase) starts the real NotebookApp and drives it over HTTP: GET/POST /login with a crafted post-sign-in destination, a verbatim origin-form GET request target ending in a slash, and GET / with a configured landing address.
sites: notebook/auth/login.py:42-59 (_redirect_safe parses the target and reasons about the parsed path while the browser resolves the raw string)
notebook/base/handlers.py:858-867 (TrailingSlashHandler copies request.uri into Location after stripping a trailing slash)
notebook/notebookapp.py:1393-1395 (default_url is trusted when it starts with base_url) and :1740 (the open-page slice depends on that prefix)
routes: T1: POST /login with next=///host/... or next=/\host/... -> 302 Location resolved by the browser to another host
T2: GET //host/some/dir/ (verbatim request target) -> TrailingSlashHandler 302 Location //host/some/dir
T3: GET / with default_url=//host/start (base_url '/') -> RedirectWithParams 302 Location //host/start

reproduced_on_pinned.T1: next='///redirect.invalid/landing' -> Location '///redirect.invalid/landing'; next='/\\redirect.invalid/landing' -> raw backslash Location

verified.project_tests_run: notebook/auth/tests/test_login.py: 2 tests pass at the pinned commit inside the image and again on the restored tree in the verifier
verified.local_runs: One project image, pinned tree: 6/6 security fail and 10/10 functional pass (including the 2 project login tests). solution/fix.patch: 16/16 pass. miss_T1/T2/T3 each leave only that concept's 2 security tests failing with all functional passing. upstream_first_fix (the rest of A's published login fix) leaves 5 security tests failing. upstream_fix (all published login fixes applied together) leaves 4 security tests failing (T2 and T3). unlisted_route leaves 4 security failing. crash_as_refusal leaves 2 security failing (500 is not a refusal). check_after_adjustment leaves 1 security failing. refuse_all breaks 8 functional tests. hardening and alternative pass 16/16.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected outcome is the destination of a redirect, not a resource identity, so there is no neighbouring object to decide on
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles or directions; each redirect site is required independently and is proven by its own miss check
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the task is about the destination a response sends the browser to; there is no read/write split
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no parser-produced identity or name takes part in the decision
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority, secret or role lookup takes part in the decision
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference keeps every existing public API and handler signature; it adds no new required argument

traps.shape: browser-resolved shape: the login check reasons about urlparse's path while the browser resolves the raw string; a leading run of slashes, or a backslash, has an empty netloc yet still names an authority
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the advisory's own incomplete fix is the pinned state

traps.shape: route where no target validation ever existed: the trailing-slash handler copies the origin-form request target into Location after stripping a trailing slash, so a target that begins with two slashes becomes a scheme-relative redirect
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the handler and its first-priority route are the pinned product's own

traps.shape: stored configuration trusted by a prefix test: the configured landing address is rebased only when it does not start with the server prefix, so a scheme-relative value is stored and mounted as the root redirect while still passing the prefix test
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the landing-address rebase and the open-page slice are the pinned product's own

a.summary: parse the login redirect target and reject a netloc, then escape backslashes so Chrome cannot read one as a slash (the 5.7.x variants are 70fe9f0d and c6fafc38c)

b.summary: complete A: treat any value whose authority-free rendering differs from the raw value as a full URL, allow only the same origin or a configured cross-origin origin, and keep the empty-netloc and backslash forms out

history.pinned_rule: the build prompt and the reader record pin the commit that contains A's first fix (the state B's advisory calls incomplete), not its parent: b9d9e65 is 'parse urls when validating redirect targets', and its login.py is exactly the A code the reader describes. upstream_first_fix.patch therefore adds the remaining published A commit on top of this state, and upstream_fix.patch adds A plus B.
